topology: one GitHub x86 VM with original TLS, Rust TUN/AF_PACKET and three actual Linux netns; not physical WAN or Windows

first_native_action.detail: product original Go TLS and accelerated Rust release compile passed, separate routing Rust unit mistakenly requested native FEC feature; fixed by testing isolated route logic without the unrelated ISA-L native test dependency; no TCP executed in failed run

conclusion.what_worked: Candidate cold single-route gate reduced Rust source queue full 25940/50467 to2185 and showed higher receiver goodput 319.7 vs267.8/265.6Mbps in this single same-VM unseeded GE draw.
conclusion.why_rejected: True kernel TUN device tx_dropped became38670 only during candidate, while original two phases0 and all fq qdisc drops0; loss was displaced upstream. M4 TX CPU per actual delivered GiB worsened ~14% (11.64 vs10.22 s/GiB), true max requested <=1000us sleep measured1896508ns, p99/small TCP and UDP not qualified. TCP retrans per delivered GiB not unambiguously improved.
conclusion.caveats: No exact shared loss sequence across TCP cases, one source/SOURCE x86 only, source link tx_dropped and qdisc drop different counters. The gate may delay other flows on one lease and a joining second lease during a sleeping turn. Product full no-HOL cannot be claimed.
conclusion.next: Do not turn gate on by default. First identify source first failure without hiding local loss: investigate fair producer-side pacing at existing kernel TUN and original M4 consumption/wakeup including sent/kern wait under same 1% multi-flow, rather than expanding queue or outer ordered ACK wait; evaluate actual packet delivery/p99 and multi-lease promptly before platform rollout.

immutable_protocols: original standard Go TLS/TCP-like, one Rust data owner, out-of-order immediate RX delivery/no HOL, original ciphertext/PN bounded once opportunistic performative outer retransmission, FEC, AEAD/MTU/lease/generation and owned Stop remain unchanged
